title: "No one believed me": October Looms Large in Austin - NewsBreak
text:
By Nicholas Kingman ,
13 hours ago
Florida Gators defensive end Tyreak Sapp (94) and linebacker Myles Graham (5) sack Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. (Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images) As the slate stands following week four, the Texas Longhorns have seven ranked opponents left on the schedule, the most of any current team in college football.
Let’s not beat around the bush — the Longhorns are heading into a slaughterhouse in the month of October. If Oklahoma hadn’t fallen apart to open this season, Texas could have played four straight ranked teams this month.
Even with the recent history of the Red River Showdown in Dallas, rivalry game outcomes can be hard to judge because pure hatred brings out a different level of passion, skewing a surefire victory for either squad.
“This league is no joke. It’s a real league. Week in and week out, it’s like, how do you just go corral your team to say, hey, ‘I need you mentally, and I need you physically attached to this game starting on Monday,’” Steve Sarkisian said. “It’s not just the physical component of this league; it’s the mental component of this league that it requires.”
So the rest of the slate – No. 8 Florida, No. 9 Ole Miss, and No. 16 Mississippi State all masquerade their way for three season-defining games in Austin. That three-word sequence is going to get very old by the end of the season.
Gators head coach Jon Sumerall, the sport’s newest rising star, is turning a conference bottom-dweller into one of college football’s biggest threats. They seem to be getting better as the weeks go on.
Florida is cruising down Main Street with the best statistical running back in the SEC, Jaden Baugh, and a 4-0 record – notably with a fourth-quarter brutalization of Ole Miss last week.
If Texas drops any game, that’s the one, especially given their lackluster follow-up performances after Red River in the last two years.
“I tried to tell you guys about Florida last year. No one believed me,” Sarkisian said. “They got real players in Gainesville, and they’re a good football team, and they’ve kind of figured it out. So we’ll worry about that when that one comes.”
The Rebels are a tricky one. They’ve certainly shown they can perform in crunch time – Trinidad Chambliss is a miracle worker on the football field. But their defense struggles to stop a nosebleed, let alone a competent offense.
Using the Baugh method, Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers can put up Bo Jackson video game numbers against the Ole Miss rush defense, the last in the SEC and ranked No. 126 in the country as of this writing.
Mississippi State is the most intriguing game that closes out October because, like Texas, they have their own house of horrors awaiting them. Unlike Ole Miss and Florida, the Bulldogs’ current resume is mediocre at best.
If the Bulldogs go at least 2-1 against their next three opponents—Alabama, LSU, and Oklahoma—it’ll be a different story come Halloween Night at DKR.
Kamario Taylor is a weapon, just as dangerous as his Magnolia State counterpart, and Converse, Texas native Anthony Evans III is breaking out this season. The Bulldogs’ weak point is their pass defense: South Carolina’s LaNorris Sellers and Missouri’s Austin Simmons posted 290 yards in the air and a combined five passing touchdowns.
See a funny trend with the Mississippi schools?
Regardless, there won’t be many treats in the Longhorns candy bucket — it’ll be a bunch of tricks testing Texas’ might. Fortunately, the schedule flipped this season, and all of these games will be played on friendly ground.
“16 wins versus top 25 teams since 2023, which is more than any other team in the country,” Sarkisian said. “We take a lot of we take a lot of pride in that. Of those 16 teams, six of those were top 10 ranked teams.”
